meta.title: The Story Engine: An Entrepreneur's Guide to Content Strategy and Brand Storytelling Without Spending All Day Writing
meta.author: Kyle Gray

parts.title: Why Content Marketing with The Story Engine

sentences: The introduction to *The Story Engine* shares **Tom Morkes’ thoughts** on content marketing as a **powerful** yet often **overlooked tool**.
Many shy away because it’s **hard** to create captivating content and seeing **returns** takes **time**.
However, **Kyle Gray’s book** offers a **strategy** to succeed in content marketing.
Tom shares his journey, explaining that **great content** gains value over time, and introduces Kyle's experiences with WP Curve.
The book provides a **playbook** to handle the challenges in content creation and helps turn it into a **manageable process** for business growth.

parts.title: The Invisible Value of Content Marketing

sentences: **Content marketing** is unconventional in digital marketing.
It contributes to **brand building** and **relationship building** beyond measurable outcomes like sales or conversions.
This change in perspective emphasizes **relationships over immediate ROI**.
Some results, like inspiring fans, recruiting talent, or attracting partners, can't be tracked traditionally but offer significant value.
**Patrick Hourihan** notes content's role in a **fluid, non-linear purchase cycle**.
Shifting to see content's broader impact encourages **trust building** and can lead to unexpected opportunities.
**Alex Turnbull** from GrooveHQ highlights content's power in creating fans who advocate for the brand even if they're not direct customers.
**Dan Norris’s** partnership formation for WP Curve illustrates content's role in collaboration.
Success in content marketing isn't immediate but stems from a **long-term relationship strategy**.

parts.title: The Importance of a Well-Documented Content Strategy

sentences: Having a **content strategy** gives your business an edge.
Out of B2B marketers, **53% of the most effective** have a documented strategy, compared to **40% of the least effective** with no strategy.
Without a written plan, your content direction may not align with your goals, similar to how a phone description of a landscape rarely matches the image in your mind when someone draws it.
This highlights the importance of clearly writing down your strategy to ensure everyone is aligned and to **improve** it over time.
Developing a **well-documented strategy** involves answering key questions about your content mission and target audience.
For instance, your content should not just aim to **get more customers** but have a broader vision that resonates above sales.
Using tools like **empathy maps** can help you understand what's happening in the minds of your audience.
This understanding should guide your content creation, ensuring it aligns with the **core problems** your audience faces, which is crucial for long-term success.
**Relationships** are crucial for early wins in **content marketing**.
**Networking** with **influencers** can drive initial **traffic** to your site, so it's important to build these connections consistently.
As campaigns progress, target more significant personalities and collaborations might come your way.
Use a **system** to track interactions to avoid losing valuable connections amid distractions.
Even for an extrovert, structure helps visualize and manage your network.

Seek out **influencers** by asking current **followers**, using social media tools like **Followerwonk** and **Littlebird**, or exploring **Facebook groups** and **podcasts** to identify influential personalities.
**Images** Large images can slow **load times**, hurt SEO, and affect **reader experience**.
Always use images sized to fit their intended display size to avoid pixelation or blurring.
**Image formats**: 1.
**JPEG**: Best for photos.
**PNG**: Ideal for screenshots.
**GIF**: Great for animations.
Size control is crucial for site speed, impacts search traffic, and hosting costs.

parts.title: Chapter 11 - Becoming a Content Idea Machine

paragraphs.heading: Chapter 11 - Becoming a Content Idea Machine
sentences: Generating **content ideas** can be challenging initially, but it doesn’t have to be groundbreaking.
Your **customers** might be unaware of other **businesses'** content.
The key is **consistency**.
Find a **rhythm** by batching idea generation.
**Experiment** with drafting consistently, even if it feels less inspiring.
Once **writing** becomes a **habit**, it gets easier.
Remember, approaches to a **topic** can be varied.
Try experimenting with different tones or **angles**.
Focus on **broad themes** for extended periods, and observe what works for **competitors**.

parts.title: Enhancing Blog Engagement with Visual Content

sentences: **Visual content** is crucial for creating a distinct look and feel for your blog, setting you apart from others.
A unique **art style** adds personality in a way that content alone cannot.
Blogs like "**Wait But Why**" use simple **stick figure illustrations** to effectively communicate ideas, despite their "low budget" appearance.
The blog masterfully uses visual content to **clarify ideas**, add **comic relief**, and **break up long posts**, making it more engaging for readers.
The use of recurring **characters**, like AdEspresso's blog mascot, creates **consistency** and makes the content **relatable** to followers.
However, it's essential that visuals **resonate with your audience**, as the **Empire Flippers** learned when they had to eliminate cartoon visuals that damaged customer trust.
Upon rebranding with a minimalist look, they experienced more growth, highlighting the importance of fitting visuals to **audience expectations**.
**Involve your team** in content marketing to make it more interesting and connect better with customers.
By sharing stories and insights from multiple team members, you enhance content depth and make your brand more relatable.
It's crucial to educate your team on the **value of content marketing** so they buy into the campaign.
Share **goals, case studies, and your vision** to engage them.
Encourage contribution by making it **easy to share ideas** through templates or regular brainstorm sessions.
Build a **knowledge base** where team expertise is stored, offering valuable insights for content.
**Team-generated content**, such as community posts or roundups, can highlight company culture and strengthen team involvement.
Finally, ensure simple methods for the **team to promote content** via email notifications, enabling collective social media reach.
It is important to hire writers to boost content creation without overwhelming entrepreneurs.
**Platforms** like Problogger, Zerys, Upwork, and **guest blogs** are suggested for finding skilled writers.
It's essential to find writers who are **native speakers**, have **engagement** in their prior work, and are **capable of meeting deadlines**.
Bonus skills include **SEO understanding**, **design**, and **social media strategies**.
When hiring writers, compensation should be agreed upon **per article** and vary based on **industry standard and expertise**.
Writers should start with one article and can be assigned more work as trust builds.
Pay rates generally range from **$70-$350** for developed articles.
Additional considerations like **technical knowledge** of a topic can influence pay.
**Make sure** your writers have everything they **need** to do their job without too much back and forth.
**Walk** them through the content strategy, style guide, keyword bank, and key relationships.
**Emphasize** the importance of the style guide in their work and encourage **questions** and **comments** for clarity.
**Start** new writers with well-defined tasks to minimize **interpretation errors**.
As they become familiar with your system, gradually **increase** their freedom in research and topic selection.
When proposing a blog post, provide a **summary**, and links to relevant **content**.
Consider including an **outline** or abstract highlighting key points to cover.
